chapter_notes.text: This chapter does not cover: a. disposable foot or shoe coverings of flimsy material (for example, paper, sheeting of plastics) without applied soles. These products are classified according to their constituent material; b. footwear of textile material, without an outer sole glued, sewn or otherwise affixed or applied to the upper (Section XI); c. worn footwear of heading 6309; d. articles of asbestos (heading 6812); e. orthopaedic footwear or other orthopaedic appliances, or parts thereof (heading 9021); or f. toy footwear or skating boots with ice or roller skates attached; shin-guards or similar protective sportswear (Chapter 95).

For the purposes of heading 6406, the term 'parts' does not include pegs, protectors, eyelets, hooks, buckles, ornaments, braid, laces, pompons or other trimmings (which are to be classified in their appropriate headings) or buttons or other goods of heading 9606.

For the purposes of this Chapter: a. the terms 'rubber' and 'plastics' include woven fabrics or other textile products with an external layer of rubber or plastics being visible to the naked eye; for the purpose of this provision, no account should be taken of any resulting change of colour; and b. the term 'leather' refers to the goods of heading 4107 and 4112 to 4114.

Subject to Note 3 to this chapter: a. the material of the upper shall be taken to be the constituent material having the greatest external surface area, no account being taken of accessories or reinforcements such as ankle patches, edging, ornamentation, buckles, tabs, eyelet stays or similar attachments; b. the constituent material of the outer sole shall be taken to be the material having the greatest surface area in contact with the ground, no account being taken of accessories or reinforcements such as spikes, bars, nails, protectors or similar attachments.

subheading_notes.text: For the purposes of subheadings 6402 12, 6402 19, 6403 12, 6403 19 and 6404 11, the expression 'sports footwear' applies only to: a. footwear which is designed for a sporting activity and has, or has provision for the attachment of, spikes, sprigs, stops, clips, bars or the like; b. skating boots, ski-boots and cross-country ski footwear, snowboard boots, wrestling boots, boxing boots and cycling shoes.

definitions.text: Per Chapter Note 4(a): the material of the upper shall be taken to be the constituent material having the greatest external surface area, no account being taken of accessories or reinforcements such as ankle patches, edging, ornamentation, buckles, tabs, eyelet stays or similar attachments.

Per Chapter Note 4(b): the constituent material of the outer sole shall be taken to be the material having the greatest surface area in contact with the ground, no account being taken of accessories or reinforcements such as spikes, bars, nails, protectors or similar attachments.

definitions.term: rubber and plastics (extended definition for Chapter 64)
definitions.text: Per Chapter Note 3(a): the terms 'rubber' and 'plastics' include woven fabrics or other textile products with an external layer of rubber or plastics being visible to the naked eye; for the purpose of this provision, no account should be taken of any resulting change of colour.
Per Chapter Note 3(b): the term 'leather' refers to the goods of heading 4107 and 4112 to 4114.

Within the meaning of Note 4 (a), 'reinforcements' is taken to mean 'all pieces of material attached to the external surface' to provide strength. After removal, visible material must support the foot sufficiently for walking. (Source: HMRC additional chapter note, not a primary WCO HS note.)

definitions.term: textile material layers lacking durability (additional gloss on Note 4(b))
definitions.text: Within the meaning of note 4 (b), 'textile material layers lacking durability characteristics' are not considered outer soles. (Source: HMRC additional chapter note, not a primary WCO HS note.)

fetch_warnings: Section XII has NO section-level legal notes in the WCO HS — confirmed via two independent sources (UK HMRC and findhs.codes). Chapters 64-67 each carry only their own chapter notes. section_notes is intentionally empty.

Two 'Additional Chapter Notes' (the reinforcements gloss and the durability gloss on Notes 4(a)/4(b)) appear on the HMRC page as EU/UK administrative clarifications rather than core WCO HS notes. They are included in definitions[] for completeness but labelled as such.

The legally decisive definitions of 'upper', 'outer sole', 'rubber'/'plastics', and 'leather' for Chapter 64 are embedded inside Chapter Notes 3 and 4 — they are not standalone definitional notes in HS 2022. They are duplicated into definitions[] for ease of lookup.
